skill.name: vercel-react-view-transitions
skill.description: Implement native React view transitions for navigation, shared elements, lists, and loading states. Includes Next.js integration, CSS recipes, accessibility guidance, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Add purposeful React and Next.js animations with native view transitions and reduced-motion support.

content.value_statement: Navigation and loading updates can lose visual continuity or create distracting motion. This skill guides agents through purposeful React transitions, Next.js integration, and accessible CSS.
actual_capabilities: Audit navigation triggers, Suspense boundaries, shared visuals, and persistent controls before selecting transition patterns.
Implement shared element morphs with unique names and separate keyed boundaries for list identity.
Configure directional hierarchical navigation and independent Suspense reveal animations.
Animate list reordering, component appearance, tab indicators, and layout displacement using React transitions.
Integrate Next.js navigation types, route prefetching, and Server Component transition boundaries.
Provide CSS recipes, reduced-motion rules, Web Animations event examples, and symptom-based troubleshooting.
limitations: Requires compatible React or Next.js APIs; verify availability against the installed runtime and documentation.
Unsupported browsers skip animations, and supported browsers retain snapshot, scrolling, and hit-testing limitations.
Shared morphs require matching elements in the same transition; unresolved destination content cannot form a pair.
Nested boundaries do not independently enter or exit when their parent mounts or unmounts as one unit.

use_cases.title: Connect Product Lists and Details
use_cases.description: Animate product images between catalog and detail views while keeping navigation controls stationary.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers building React commerce interfaces

use_cases.title: Coordinate Streamed Route Updates
use_cases.description: Separate route navigation from loading reveals and verify shared elements with production prefetching.

use_cases.title: Review Motion Accessibility
use_cases.description: Check reduced-motion handling, transition purpose, persistent controls, and interaction behavior during animations.

prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: implement visual continuity across hierarchical navigation.

prompt_templates.prompt: In [Next.js application], verify installed APIs and implement typed navigation plus independent Suspense reveals. Check destination readiness and production prefetch behavior.

prompt_templates.prompt: Debug [transition issue] across every navigation path. Check boundary placement, duplicate names, default settings, optimistic state, and hit-testing. Implement fixes and report verification.

output_examples.input: Audit a catalog with product details, category tabs, and loading skeletons.
output: Catalog to detail: shared image morph with forward navigation.
Detail to catalog: explicit return navigation with a back transition type.
Category tabs: crossfade without directional slides.
Loading completion: independent reveal without navigation types.
Persistent header: isolate from page motion.

output_examples.input: Explain why a shared image does not morph after navigation.
output_examples.output: The destination image remains behind an unresolved loading boundary. Prefetch and cache its data, or keep a separate reveal when it becomes available.

output_examples.input: Review a sortable favorites list that makes recommendations jump.
output_examples.output: Keep keyed item boundaries update-enabled. Wrap the displaced recommendations as an immediate sibling boundary, and drive ordering from committed state.

best_practices: Audit all navigation and loading paths, then implement every applicable pattern with a clear continuity or spatial purpose.
Use unique shared names, preserve keyed list identity, and opt into only the triggers each boundary needs.
Include reduced-motion CSS and verify production behavior with cold caches, persistent controls, and active popovers.
anti_patterns: Using directional slides for unordered tabs or adding animations without a clear spatial or continuity purpose.
Disabling all defaults on keyed lists without restoring update behavior, or expecting untyped Suspense reveals to match navigation types.
Reusing shared names across simultaneously mounted surfaces or placing page transitions inside a competing layout boundary.

faq.question: Does this skill include an animation library?
faq.answer: No. It supplies implementation guidance, examples, and CSS recipes for React and browser view transition APIs.

faq.question: Which runtime does it require?
faq.answer: Use a runtime that exposes ViewTransition and the required navigation APIs. Verify compatibility against installed React or Next.js documentation.

faq.question: Will animations work in every browser?
faq.answer: No. Unsupported browsers skip animations. Verify supported browser behavior and retain usable navigation without motion.

faq.question: Why does a shared element sometimes fail to morph?
faq.answer: Both named elements must participate in the same transition. Duplicate names, disabled share behavior, missing types, or unresolved content can prevent pairing.

faq.question: Does browser back preserve directional transition types?
faq.answer: No. Browser history navigation carries no transition types. Use explicit typed navigation for directional motion; untyped shared morphs can still apply.

faq.question: How does the skill address reduced motion?
faq.answer: It includes a global prefers-reduced-motion rule that sets transition animation duration and delay to zero.
